Have a vision-language model suggest names for sniglets

Source: R/suggest-names.R
suggestSnigletNames.Rd

A sniglet starts with a coined word ("dulmzil") because nobody has looked at it yet. This function does the first look for you: it shows a vision-language model each sniglet's example crops (and, for contrast, crops from photos in which the sniglet was not found, when there are any) and asks for a short name and a one-sentence definition. The result is a names table for renameSniglets(), so naming becomes reviewing suggestions instead of writing every name from scratch. Nothing is renamed until you pass the table (or the CSV file) to renameSniglets().

Usage

suggestSnigletNames(
  x,
  model,
  vision = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  scores = NULL,
  crops = NULL,
  sniglets = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  examples = 4,
  contrast = 4,
  maxWords = 3,
  retries = 2,
  file = NULL,
  pause = 0,
  size = 96,
  resume = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A key from keyFromSniglets(), or a discoverSniglets() result.

model

The vision-language model: a function function(images, prompt) that returns the model's reply as text. images is a list with one entry per crop, each a list with data (the image, base64 encoded), mediaType (e.g. "image/png") and role ("example" or "contrast"); the examples come first. claudeNamer() makes such a function for the Anthropic API.

vision, images

A visionModel() and the imageSet() the sniglets were found in, to cut crops when x does not carry them.

scores

Optional images x sniglets matrix from snigletScores(), used to pick contrast crops for a sniglet set.

crops

Optional crops of your own: a list named by coined word, each entry either a character vector of examples or a list with examples and contrast. A crop is an image file, a data: URI or a base64 string.

sniglets

Which sniglets to name (coined words or current names). By default the ones a key uses, or all of a sniglet set.

labels

The class names, which a sniglet name must not contain. By default the key's results, or the labels of images.

examples, contrast

How many example and contrast crops to show per sniglet at most.

maxWords

Longest name allowed, in words.

retries

How many times to ask again when a name cannot be used.

file

Optional path of a CSV file to write the table to. It is the spreadsheet renameSniglets() reads: review it, edit the name and definition columns, then renameSniglets(x, file). It is written after every sniglet.

pause

Seconds to wait between sniglets, for APIs with a rate limit.

size

Size in pixels of crops cut with vision.

resume

TRUE to carry on from an existing file instead of starting again; see "Long runs".

Value

A data frame with one row per sniglet, in the shape renameSniglets() takes: sniglet (the coined word), name and definition (the suggestion, or what the sniglet already had when there is no usable suggestion), followed by status ("ok", "suffixed", "rejected", "error" or "no crops") and note. renameSniglets() ignores the last two columns.

Where the crops come from

  • A key that has been through patchExemplars() carries its crops, so nothing else is needed. The contrast crops are those of the key's "Lacks" leads.

  • For a key without crops, or a discoverSniglets() result, give vision and images and the crops are cut for you. For a sniglet set, scores (from snigletScores()) adds contrast crops: the best-matching region of the photos that match the sniglet least.

  • Or give your own in crops.

What makes a usable name

Each suggestion is checked, and the model is asked again (up to retries times, with the reason) when a name

  • has more than maxWords words (a leading "a", "an" or "the" is not counted);

  • contains the name of one of the classes (labels), also in the plural: a sniglet is something you can see on a specimen, such as "a serrate margin", not the species it was found on. For labels written "Common name (Genus species)" the common name, the scientific name and the genus are all refused, and so is the last word of a common name of several words ("aspen" of "Quaking aspen", so "aspen bark" is refused), unless every class ends in it or it is a general word such as "tree" or "flower";

  • is already the name or the coined word of another sniglet. Capitals, punctuation and a leading article make no difference: "Serrate margin" and "a serrate margin" are the same name;

  • is no name at all ("unknown", "n/a", or nothing but punctuation).

A leading "has" or "lacks" is taken off first, since the key adds its own.

If the last answer is still a duplicate it gets a number ("peeling bark 2", status "suffixed"). If it still breaks another rule, or the model fails (an API error, a rate limit, a refusal, a reply that cannot be read), the sniglet keeps the name it had and the row says why in status and note; the other sniglets are not affected.

Long runs

With file, the table is written after every sniglet, so a run that is interrupted or stopped by an error leaves what it had. resume = TRUE picks such a file up: sniglets it already has a usable name for (status "ok" or "suffixed") are not asked about again, the others are. Without resume an existing file is overwritten. The folder of file must exist.

See also

claudeNamer(), renameSniglets(), snigletNames()

Examples

set.seed(1)
patches <- array(rnorm(5 * 9 * 8), c(5, 9, 8))
patches <- sweep(patches, c(1, 2), sqrt(apply(patches^2, c(1, 2), sum)), "/")
s <- discoverSniglets(patches, k = 2)
pics <- imageSet(system.file("extdata", "pics", package = "dimoose"))
crops <- stats::setNames(list(pics$path[1:2], pics$path[3:4]), s$sniglets$sniglet)
# a stand-in for a real model, which would look at the crops
replies <- c('{"name": "a waxy skin", "definition": "Smooth skin with a dull shine."}',
             '{"name": "a ribbed surface", "definition": "Parallel ridges along the fruit."}')
asked <- 0
fake <- function(images, prompt) { asked <<- asked + 1; replies[asked] }
suggestions <- suggestSnigletNames(s, fake, crops = crops, labels = unique(pics$label))
suggestions
#>         sniglet             name                       definition status note
#> 1     gaithiark      a waxy skin   Smooth skin with a dull shine.     ok     
#> 2 treuxraikbluk a ribbed surface Parallel ridges along the fruit.     ok     
snigletNames(renameSniglets(s, suggestions))
#>         sniglet             name                       definition
#> 1     gaithiark      a waxy skin   Smooth skin with a dull shine.
#> 2 treuxraikbluk a ribbed surface Parallel ridges along the fruit.
